llc.formation_notes: $15 handling fee only for in-person counter filings. Initial Statement of Information due within 90 days of formation. The first-year $800 tax exemption applied only to tax years 2021-2023 and has expired.

annual_report.name: Statement of Information (Form LLC-12)
annual_report.due: Within 90 days of formation, then every two years by the end of the filing period (month of formation)
annual_report.late_penalty: $250 penalty for failure to file (collected by FTB for the Secretary of State)

state_tax_on_llc.name: Annual LLC tax
state_tax_on_llc.applies: Every LLC doing business in or organized/registered in California, including single-member disregarded LLCs
state_tax_on_llc.notes: Due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the tax year (Form FTB 3522), owed every year until the LLC is cancelled. No first-year exemption after 2023 (except short-form cancellation within one year).

state_tax_on_llc.name: LLC fee (gross receipts)
state_tax_on_llc.applies: LLCs with total California income of $250,000 or more

sources.quote: $20 for California nonprofit corporations and all limited liability companies.

entity_level_taxes.name: S corporation franchise tax
entity_level_taxes.notes: 1.5% of California net income, $800 minimum franchise tax. The minimum tax is waived for a newly formed or qualified S corp's first taxable year (the 1.5% still applies to first-year income).

pte_elective_tax.rate_note: PTE elective tax 9.3% of qualified net income; extended to taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 and before January 1, 2031. For 2026-2030, missing the June 15 payment no longer voids the election, but owners' credit is reduced by 12.5% of the unpaid amount.

sources.title: S corporations | FTB.ca.gov
sources.quote: We tax every S corporation that has California source income 1.5%.

sources.title: Pass-through entity elective tax | FTB.ca.gov
sources.quote: The PTE elective tax is 9.3% of the qualified entity's qualified net income

personal_exemption.notes: Personal exemption credit $158 single / $316 joint; dependent exemption credit $491 (2026, CCPI 3.4%). Credits phase out at higher incomes.

income_tax_2026.surtaxes: 1% Mental Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000 (all filing statuses, not indexed), making the top rate 13.3%. Employees also pay SDI 1.3% on all wages (2026); self-employed are not covered unless they opt in.

estimated_tax.required_if: You expect to owe at least $500 ($250 if married/RDP filing separately) after withholding and credits
estimated_tax.notes: California schedule is 30% / 40% / 0% / 30%: no payment due on September 15. High earners (AGI $1,000,000+, $500,000 MFS) must base payments on current-year tax.

unemployment_2026.notes: New employers 3.4% UI for two to three years; 2026 schedule F+ (1.5%-6.2%). Plus ETT 0.1% on first $7,000. Employee SDI 1.3% on all wages (2026).

local_taxes.name: Gross Receipts Tax (and Overpaid Executive Tax)
local_taxes.applies: Businesses with San Francisco gross receipts above the small business exemption; rates depend on business activity category (7 categories since Proposition M, 2024). All businesses must still pay the annual Business Registration Fee.
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Small business exemption: $5 million of San Francisco gross receipts, starting with tax year 2025 filing (due 2026); businesses at or below it do not file the GRT return. June 2, 2026 Measure C (raise to $7.5 million) failed 34.02% yes / 65.98% no.
local_taxes.quote: Increases the Gross Receipts Tax and Overpaid Executive Tax Small Business Exemption ceiling from $2,250,000 to $5 million.

notable: Every LLC pays $800 a year even with no income, plus a gross-receipts LLC fee from $250,000 of California income (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/limited-liability-company/index.html)
Estimated payments are front-loaded: 30% April, 40% June, nothing in September, 30% January (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/estimated-tax-payments.html)
PTE elective tax renewed for 2026-2030 at 9.3% (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/credits/pass-through-entity-elective-tax/index.html)
San Francisco voters rejected raising the gross receipts small business exemption to $7.5M on June 2, 2026; it stays at $5M (https://www.sfelections.org/results/20260602/index.html)
uncertain: SF Gross Receipts Tax rates per category not recorded (rate null); whether the $5M exemption is CPI-adjusted for tax year 2026 not verified.
Other California city business taxes (Los Angeles business tax with small business exemption, Oakland, San Jose) not researched.
